comparison: Both evaluate claims C49-C54 regarding calcium imaging of CIII md and CIV md neurons. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes differential responses between neuron types and compartments, while peer reviewers acknowledge compelling evidence with high experimental rigor.

Both evaluate claims C55-C57 regarding CIII md neuron requirement for cold-evoked CT responses. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights behavioral data and controls, while peer reviewers note compelling evidence though Reviewer 3 raises specificity concerns about the driver line.

Both evaluate claims C58-C61, C63 regarding optogenetic activation of CIII md and CIV md neurons. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, noting that CIV md co-activation does not enhance CT responses. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising major concerns that downstream neurons fail to trigger CT responses when activated, questioning the CIII neuron sufficiency hypothesis.

Both evaluate claims C64-C66 regarding developmental scaling of cold-evoked CT responses. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes linear scaling consistent with developmental changes, while peer reviewers acknowledge experimental rigor and diverse phenotypes.

Both address Basin neuron involvement (C67-C69). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates a broader set of Basin claims (C34-C36, C67-C79) with comprehensive behavioral and imaging data. Peer reviewers note compelling evidence for mapping sensory and post-sensory neurons without challenging Basin silencing data.

Both address Basin co-activation claims (C70-C73). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on behavioral and calcium imaging data. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning the logic of co-activating neurons already downstream of CIII and suggesting silencing experiments during CIII activation would be more convincing.

Both address Basin calcium imaging claims (C74-C76). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader Basin imaging claims, while peer reviewers specifically note that calcium imaging experiments with optogenetics support the wiring diagram.

Both address differential Basin dynamics claims (C77-C79). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes differential dynamics between Basin-2 and Basin-4, while peer reviewers explicitly state calcium imaging experiments support the wiring diagram without challenging these specific findings.

Both evaluate claims C80-C85 regarding Goro rolling command neuron not being required for cold-evoked CT. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this distinguishes cold nociception from other modalities. Peer reviewers provide general support though Reviewer 3's co-activation critique applies broadly.

Both address premotor neuron silencing claims (C86-C89). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates broader premotor claims (C37-C38, C86-C96) with behavioral and imaging data. Peer reviewers note compelling evidence for mapping post-sensory neurons without specific challenges.

Both address premotor neuron co-activation claims (C90-C92). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on behavioral data. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning the logic of co-activating downstream neurons and suggesting silencing experiments during CIII activation.

Both address premotor neuron calcium imaging claims (C93-C94). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes calcium imaging data for DnB, while peer reviewers state calcium imaging experiments with optogenetics support the wiring diagram.

Both address DnB calcium dynamics claims (C95-C96). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes specific DnB calcium dynamics, while peer reviewers explicitly state calcium imaging experiments support the wiring diagram.

Both address projection neuron silencing claims (C97-C100). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates broader projection neuron claims (C39-C40, C97-C106) with behavioral and imaging data. Peer reviewers note compelling evidence for mapping post-sensory neurons.

Both address projection neuron co-activation claims (C101-C102). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on behavioral data. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning the co-activation logic and suggesting silencing experiments during CIII activation.

Both address A09e calcium imaging claims (C103-C104). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes calcium imaging data, while peer reviewers state calcium imaging experiments with optogenetics support the wiring diagram.

Both address TePn calcium imaging claims (C105-C106). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes calcium imaging data, while peer reviewers state calcium imaging experiments support the wiring diagram.

Both address muscle calcium imaging claims (C107-C109). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates broader muscle claims (C41-C44, C107-C113) showing segmental and muscle-group-specific patterns. Peer reviewers note experimental rigor without challenging these findings.

Both address muscle-specific calcium dynamics claims (C110-C113). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes segmental and muscle-group-specific patterns consistent with CT behavior. Peer reviewers note compelling evidence with experimental rigor.

Both evaluate claims C114-C115 regarding neural control of muscle calcium responses. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on control experiments showing motor neuron silencing reduces muscle calcium. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning whether responses are truly neural versus mechanical, noting that not all muscles are removed in preparations.

Both evaluate major findings claims C6-C12. OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED by extensive behavioral, optogenetic, and calcium imaging data. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising fundamental concerns about whether cold-evoked CT is a true sensorimotor behavior versus physiological consequence of cold exposure (chill coma), and noting that downstream neurons fail to trigger CT responses when activated. However, Reviewers 1 and 2 accept the findings as valid.
